target_customer: Gamers, many of them minors, who trade CS:GO and Ev.io skins; revenue from trade fees
problem: Peer-to-peer skin trades happen on social media and are scam-prone; minors often cannot legally cash out.
business_model: Marketplace take rate on skin trades (company claimed about $7 average per trade)

founders.name: Mathias Hermansen
previous_startups: Trendsales (Danish second hand fashion marketplace, co-founded with the team, outcome not checked)
founders.background_notes: COO and CPO of Trendsales per the YC page.

founders.name: Martin Lykke Suhr
founders.background_notes: Generalist covering coding, growth and paid marketing.

founders.name: Peter Haldbaek
founders.background_notes: Claims 20 plus years of software development.

technical_complexity.rationale: Instant trade validation required integrating with game and Steam inventory systems, plus a parental consent flow, which is moderate engineering with platform risk.

defensibility.rationale: Skin trading sites were numerous and switching was free; the parental consent system was a small compliance edge.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Valve and other platforms changed trade rules later (2025 trade protection), but no incumbent bought or copied the product; Social First, a game studio, acquired it in November 2025.

market_need_then: The company reported that 46 percent of 5,000 surveyed gamers had been scammed more than once; self reported and unverified.

branding.domain_note: Uses gamerpay.gg, a gaming style TLD rather than .com.

identity.voice_and_tone: Pitch language focused on trust and fraud protection

branding.community_and_virality: Partnered with esports team Ninjas in Pyjamas in October 2021; appears on skin marketplace review sites.

brand_strength.rationale: Descriptive name and an esports sponsorship, but no evidence that the brand drove growth.

pivots.why: Announced Dec 2022 on the YC page; reason not stated

outcome_analysis: GamerPay raised a $2M seed in October 2021 after YC S21 and was acquired by Finnish studio Social First in November 2025. A single source family (csdb.gg) and the site banner say the marketplace shut down on May 29, 2026, attributed to low traffic and unprofitable fees. The price of the deal is not public. Success and failure factors are not assigned because the shutdown cause rests on one referral funded source.
notes: CB Insights shows $130K over 4 rounds, conflicting with the $2M seed; the $2M is confirmed by a newswire release and Yahoo. Competitor results were current (2026) CS2 marketplaces (Skinport, CS.Money, SkinBaron, CSFloat), not dated near the batch, so the list is empty. The shutdown date of 2026-05-29 appears on the live site banner and csdb.gg only. Exit type is acquisition per YC status.
